recommendation: Keep the core audit commit as-is. Follow up in HL7/fhir-extensions to mark additionalImplicitRules as a modifier extension with an appropriate isModifierReason, unless FHIR-I intentionally no longer wants modifier semantics for this extension.
issue_request: FHIR-43016 is Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6. It requested repeatable Resource.implicitRules, but the final FHIR-I decision kept Resource.implicitRules singular and instead required a new additionalImplicitRules modifier extension, 0..* of type uri, plus Resource.implicitRules guidance to use that extension for additional policies.
initial_application: Core commit 2aa82993970dd5274b8bb7ced92f48801b06aea9 updated source/resource/structuredefinition-Resource.xml so Resource.implicitRules remains max 1 but points DomainResource instances with additional policies to additionalImplicitRules. Extension Pack commit 6ac5032dce8db9eeccdc79970672a5b41eb174ff created the extension definition, and 8b6c4a68cd47cdf4869b7ac5e38faf7f67d78e9e later clarified the DomainResource scope.
additional_context: Resource is active in the core build through source/fhir.ini, and the combined branch contains the core implementation commit. The extension definition is now maintained in the separate HL7/fhir-extensions checkout. That external source has the approved DomainResource context, 0..* cardinality, uri value, and ordering/prioritization comment, but the rendered Extension Pack definitions page reports the root Extension as Is Modifier false.
reconciliation: No core source files were changed. The audit commit records that the core checkout is already correct for its part of the issue and that the remaining substantive mismatch must be fixed in the Extension Pack rather than in HL7/fhir.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-43016 cites rendering-CriticalElement as an example of a rule URI that might need to be combined with another implicit policy; it was not part of this reconciliation decision.
